messages:
sara: heads-up: receiving a P1 from Support — customer reported very high tail latency for text-generation endpoints (p99 ~ 450ms vs baseline ~120ms). they started seeing it around 02:12 UTC. suspecting cache behavior after yesterday's runtime tweak.

mike: on it. can you paste the customer request pattern + which model/route? any recent deploy ids?

sara: route: /v1/generate (model:redwood-7b-client), traffic: heavy small prompts with long common prefix (system prompt + user history). deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-14_21:10 (sha: a1b2c3) touched kv-prefix caching code (prefix-key hashing + TTL changes).

nina: customer repro gist: many short requests reusing a long shared prefix but with unique session suffixes. repro steps: 1) send 120 req/s of prompt: `PROMPT_PREFIX + random_session_id + short_user_query` 2) observe p95/p99 spike in 30-90s window. shared prefix length ~3k chars.

raj: that's a classic prefix-cache churn pattern. if cache key includes full session id suffix, we won't get hits. but you said we changed hashing — maybe collision/eviction behavior changed.

mike: pulled metrics. cache_hit_ratio for kv-prefix cache dropped from 87% -> 22% at 02:12. eviction_rate spiked x8. p95 went 120ms->280ms, p99 120->450ms. memory pressure on node group increased modestly, but eviction policy seems to favor new allocations (we switched LRU->segment-LRU last deploy).

sara: logs show repeated miss + load cycle:

```
[2026-03-15T02:12:14Z] kv_prefix_cache MISS key=prefix:sha1:abcd1234:sess:xyz load_ms=34
[2026-03-15T02:12:14Z] kv_prefix_cache INSERT key=prefix:sha1:abcd1234:sess:xyz size=48kb
[2026-03-15T02:12:14Z] kv_prefix_cache EVICT key=prefix:sha1:abcd999:sess:old reason=seg-lru-rebalance
[2026-03-15T02:12:14Z] inference serve latency token_ms=18 total_ms=412
```

nina: customer on the thread is getting noisy. they included traces with repeated prefix loads. i've apologized and told them we're investigating and will follow up in 30 mins.

raj: early theory: the change to segment-LRU increased churn because our workload has a very skewed key distribution: a small set of true prefixes (should be hot) but lots of near-duplicates (session suffixes) cause the segment algorithm to treat them as fresh. also our cache-key normalization may have regressed — we now hash the entire prefix including ephemeral session token. that's a bug.

mike: agreed. quick checks: 1) grep config for `kv_prefix_normalize` -> shows `false` on nodes in canary pool, `true` on stable pool. mismatch. 2) rollback plan: revert the segment-LRU change in the canary pool to LRU and re-enable normalize on canary. canary contains ~20% traffic; should be safe.

sara: can we do a quick mitigation without rollback? options: increase cache size, bump hot-set admission threshold, warmup common prefixes, or patch normalization to strip session id suffixes before hashing. which is fastest?

raj: fastest: toggle normalize=true in runtime config -> immediate effect on new entries (we'll still have thrash for existing entries until eviction stabilizes). or prefill cache with hot prefixes (warmup) for the next 5 mins. patch to key computation needs a build+deploy (~30-45m).

mike: I'll toggle normalize flag on canary nodes now, and change eviction config to temporarily favor older entries (simulate classic LRU) via runtime flag. doing it via /admin/config: `POST /admin/config {"kv_prefix_normalize": true, "eviction_mode": "lru_bias"}`

oncall-bot: mike invoked /admin/config on 5 nodes: success (5/5)

mike: monitoring... cache_hit_ratio climbing: 22% -> 72% in 90s, eviction_rate down. p95 trending down to ~140ms. p99 down to ~190ms.

sara: nice. nina please update customer: we found a cache-key normalization mismatch in a canary and applied a config fix; looking stable but continuing to observe.

nina: updated. customer appreciates the rapid response. asked for root-cause and long-term fix ETA.

raj: for RCA: two items: 1) config drift: canary nodes didn't pick up normalize flag — cause: deploy config template not applied during automated rollout. 2) algorithmic mismatch: segment-LRU is suboptimal for our workload with many near-duplicate keys. recommended long-term fixes: canonicalize keys to remove session-specific suffixes upstream, revert to LRU or use GDSF with size-aware admission, and add prewarming for known hot prefixes during deploys.

mike: action items: - roll canary back to LRU permanently for now (pj#789) - add a prewarm job in deploy pipeline to seed top-1k prefixes (pj#790) - fix deploy templating so `kv_prefix_normalize` is set consistently (ops-issue#456) - add alert for cache_hit_ratio drop below 60% (alert#1223)

sara: i'm going to create a short blameless postmortem and link to this thread. Nina, we'll include a customer-facing timeline and follow-up.

nina: customer follow-up sent with timeline + mitigation steps. they asked about SLA credits; passed to sales/success.

raj: quick dev note for repro: here's a small script to reproduce locally (use with care):

```
# reproduce-churn.sh
for i in $(seq 1 500); do
  id=$(head /dev/urandom | tr -dc A-Za-z0-9 | head -c 8)
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT" -d "{\"prompt\": \"COMMON_PREFIX_${id} hello\"}" &
done
```

sara: notes for postmortem: include metrics snapshot, the exact deploy id, timeline of config drift detection, and customer impact window. recommend we add e2e test in CI that runs a small prefix-churn scenario against canary config.

mike: all actions logged to pj#789/790. i'll schedule the LRU revert for the next deploy window (in 30m). if anyone sees p99 climb again, ping @mike and @raj immediately.

deploy-bot: scheduled revert deploy 2026-03-15T03:00Z (deploy id: revert-lru-179123).

sara: thanks team. closing the emergency unless new signals pop. will convert to postmortem task list after revert completes. :thumbsup:

nina: closing customer loop and flagging for success team.

mike: post-deploy check: p99 stable at ~120-150ms, hit_ratio ~88%. marking incident mitigated.

sara: excellent. follow-ups for next week: - implement key canonicalization - deploy prewarm job - improve canary templating and add CI e2e.

nina: added follow-ups to customer ticket.

sara: thread archived for RCA write-up.
